llm.summary: This skill mostly fits its Appcues automation purpose, but it under-labels an action that can change live Appcues content.

dimensions.detail: Allowed tool access is scoped to `Bash(oo *)`, matching the stated OOMOL connector workflow rather than broad shell access.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill may install the oo CLI with a remote install script only after `oo` is missing, and otherwise uses normal OOMOL login/connection setup.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions say untagged actions are safe reads, but `unpublish_flow` is untagged even though it changes publication state.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No background persistence, local credential harvesting, or long-running worker behavior is described; credentials are stated to be handled server-side by OOMOL.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill is coherently focused on Appcues operations through the OOMOL oo CLI, including reading flows/tags and publishing or unpublishing flows.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing if your Appcues account controls production user experiences. Treat both publishing and unpublishing flows as state-changing actions that should require explicit confirmation, even though the artifact only marks publishing as `[write]`.
llm.findings:
[SDI-4] unexpected: Confirmed from the artifact: `unpublish_flow` is listed without a write/destructive tag while the safety section treats untagged actions as read-only and safe to run directly.
[SQP-1] expected: The broad Appcues routing is partly expected for an integration skill, but it compounds the concern because the same skill includes write-capable actions and one mutating action is not clearly gated.
